html:
Iran's security stance escalated significantly today as multiple oil tankers were reported ablaze in the Strait of Hormuz after hitting mines, while Tehran simultaneously threatened to strike US bases in Europe if attacked and reiterated its refusal to surrender enriched uranium. These developments coincide with US President Trump stating the US does not need a deal with Iran and suggesting the "Iran war is effectively over militarily," though reports indicate US Treasury chief Bessent has been relocated due to Iranian threats.

Russia-Ukraine: US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met Vladimir Putin in Moscow after US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi and are now meeting Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Dublin to advance peace efforts. The Abu Dhabi talks resulted in a prisoner exchange agreement, and President Putin has reportedly agreed to European negotiators joining future rounds. However, President Zelenskyy warned European leaders to be wary of US-Russia discussions on broader security arrangements for the continent. Military tensions persist, with a Russian warship hit by a Ukrainian drone in the Gulf of Finland, reportedly the first such attack in the Baltic Sea. Analysts suggest a negotiated settlement remains unlikely due to Russia's territorial demands and an increasingly pro-Moscow American approach to mediation.

Global Economy & Tech: The tech world was significantly impacted by the resignation of Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO, following revelations of alleged extramarital affairs, including one with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy and two company employees. Nvidia's chief financial officer, Colette Kress, will replace Huang on an interim basis. The scandal surrounding the "rockstar of AI" has implications for the company and the global AI race, with discussions reportedly underway in the White House about the future of Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, in light of the spy scandal and earlier reports that the Trump administration had held off from blacklisting several Chinese AI and chip companies.

Middle East Security & Humanitarian Crisis: The Israeli-Palestinian conflict continues to generate significant humanitarian and security concerns. An Israeli strike on Nasser Hospital in southern Gaza killed at least six Palestinians, including a surgeon and a child, according to health officials, marking the deadliest single strike since Israel's elections last month. As winter storms bring flooding and deadly landslides to thousands living in tents in Gaza, aid groups and UNICEF are calling on Israel to allow shelters and basin repairs, warning of severe humanitarian emergency. Separately, Houthis claim attacks on Saudi energy and military infrastructure, though Saudi Arabia has not yet commented.

Global Climate Action: International efforts to address the climate crisis faced renewed challenges as China ruled out hosting the Cop33 UN climate summit in 2028, a decision disappointing to experts who had hoped the world's largest emitter would take a global lead. This comes as the US under Donald Trump is described as having "vacated all forms of international cooperation on the climate," and Greta Thunberg told the Cop31 climate summit that the planet "is being killed."

UK-Europe Relations: The UK prime minister, Andy Burnham, expressed optimism about a "win-win" deal with the EU, suggesting it could be "more like the Brexit that people thought they were voting for in 2016." These comments came from the European Political Community summit in Dublin, ahead of an anticipated EU-UK summit next week where the prime minister hopes to bring Britain closer to Europe. Domestically, the communities secretary, Angela Rayner, has granted planning approval for an asylum center in Piddington, Oxfordshire, despite local opposition, though final Home Office approval is still needed.

US Domestic Developments: In US domestic news, Scott Colom narrowly won the Mississippi Senate race after more than a week of ballot counting. The White House has issued warnings to Democrats planning future investigations into the administration, amidst a Republican push to confirm judicial nominees before the Senate leadership change. Washington D.C. also saw a shooting at a gym where suspect Matt Wade Lambert, 55, died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound after killing James Stuart, the building manager with whom he had an ongoing dispute, and injuring four others. In New York, a building collapse in Brooklyn killed at least eight people, including two children and six adults, and injured 18.
